facts.raw_span: A 55-year-old man underwent right hemicolectomy for moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
staged as IIIB (T4N1M0)
He had no thrombophilic disorders
Preoperative carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and CA19-9 levels were normal
He completed six months of adjuvant chemotherapy
Thirteen months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
hepatitis B and C serologies were negative
Tumor markers including CEA, CA19-9, α-fetoprotein, and PIVKA-II were all within normal limits
CTA demonstrated a liver tumor with two components: a solid portion that enhanced in the early phase and washed out in the delayed phase, and a cystic component
CTAP showed absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect throughout the right lobe, suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography showed no communication with the biliary tree
bile cytology was negative for malignancy

concepts.why: The patient has a history of colon cancer and now has a liver lesion with characteristics suggestive of metastasis.
CTAP shows absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect, suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus.
The liver tumor has a solid and cystic component, which could be consistent with primary liver cancer.
The liver tumor has a cystic component, which could be a simple hepatic cyst.
The patient has a history of colon cancer and has completed adjuvant chemotherapy, but now has a new liver lesion.
The patient has a 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver, which could be a focal liver lesion.
The liver tumor has a solid component that enhances in the early phase and washes out in the delayed phase, which could be consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma.
The liver tumor has a cystic component, which could be an abscess.

rationales.F01: History of colon cancer increases the likelihood of colorectal cancer liver metastasis and colon cancer recurrence.
rationales.F02: Stage IIIB colon cancer suggests a higher risk of recurrence and metastasis.
rationales.F06: A new liver lesion is highly suggestive of metastasis, especially in a patient with a history of colon cancer.
rationales.F09: The liver tumor's characteristics, such as enhancement in the early phase and washout in the delayed phase, are consistent with metastasis or hepatocellular carcinoma.
rationales.F10: The presence of a portal vein tumor thrombus is highly suggestive of an aggressive tumor, such as hepatocellular carcinoma or colorectal cancer liver metastasis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon and the presence of a liver tumor with characteristics suggestive of metastasis support this diagnosis.
